_comment: Hook paths must be absolutised through $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. With a relative path, any shell whose cwd is not the repository root (a worktree, a subagent scratch directory, a monorepo subfolder) fails to find the file, and the result is not a block but a non-blocking status code: the guard disappears silently and the command runs. An npm publish guard defeated that way removes the whole reason this repository has hooks. The `:-.` fallback exists so clients without the variable keep the previous behaviour; it is not the normal path.
_comment_permissions: Deny rules are the one guard that needs no path to resolve and no workspace trust: Claude Code applies them immediately and evaluates them ahead of ask, allow, and any PreToolUse hook. Two standing rules — `local-first.md` "never scan password, credential, or key files from the user's disk" and `forbidden.md` "never commit service accounts, API keys, or .env* files" — had no mechanism at all. .gitignore stops a secret being committed; nothing stopped one being read into a transcript and sent to a model. The .env names are enumerated rather than globbed because a deny rule cannot carry an exception and `.env.example` is tracked, documented, and scanned by the source-language gate. `tests/contract/secret-read-guard.contract.test.ts` derives the list from .gitignore so the two cannot drift. Key material (*.pem, *.p8, *.p12, *.key, SSH keys) and the credential stores a session could reach (the release signing folder, gh, npm, netrc, AWS) are denied wherever they sit; scripts/claude-hooks.test.mjs holds the Codex secret-read hook to the same list.
_comment_effort: Opus 5.5 starts at medium, and a user-level effortLevel no longer applies to it, so the lead session that plans and judges would run at medium. xhigh is the highest level a settings file accepts; `/effort max` raises one session. Agent `effort:` frontmatter still overrides this per type (implementer low, planner and reviewer max). Never set CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL: it outranks that frontmatter. docs/engineering/agent-effort.md
